# Extract Wisdom

> Pull the durable, surprising, and actionable content out of a long piece so a reader gets more than a summary.

## Done means
- Every idea captured is one the source actually argues, not one the topic suggests.
- Ideas are stated in full sentences that make sense to someone who never saw the source.
- At least one claim the source makes that is contestable is flagged as contestable.
- Nothing generic survives. If an item would be true of any piece on this topic, cut it.
- Quotes are verbatim and attributed to a location in the source.

## Output contract
```
## In one paragraph
## Ideas            (8-20, each a complete thought)
## Insights         (3-7 — what the ideas imply that the source did not say)
## Quotes           (verbatim, with location)
## Habits or practices
## Facts and figures (with the source's own framing and any date)
## References the source recommends
## Contestable claims
## What to do about it
```

## Gotchas
Long sources hide their thesis in the middle. Read to the end before writing the first line. Resist reproducing the source's structure; organise by idea strength.
